units.title: The Eye: The Miracle of Sight
units.sub: In less than the blink of an eye after light enters it, the world takes shape in your mind.

share.v: Open my eyes, that I may see wondrous things out of your law.

blocks.h: Right now you are reading this line. Light passes through your cornea and lens and lands on the retina, a thin layer at the back of your eyeball. There it becomes electrical signals, which travel to your brain and become "seeing." All of this happens in the blink of an eye, and you do it without the slightest effort.

In very dim places, the rod cells of your eye can respond to extremely faint light. A carefully designed 2016 experiment even reported that volunteers detected a "single photon" at a rate slightly better than random guessing.
The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Yahweh has made even both of them.
From Light to Sight

items: Autofocus: The lens changes its thickness by means of the ciliary muscle around it, so it adjusts automatically whether you look near or far.
Auto-exposure: The pupil works like a camera's aperture, shrinking in bright light and widening in dim light.
Light-sensing cells: One eye has on average about 92 million rod cells (for dim light) and about 4.6 million cone cells (for color and detail), concentrated in the central "fovea."

The brain's interpretation: The image that falls on the retina is upside down, and the brain reads it right side up; the slightly different pictures from the two eyes are merged into a sense of depth; and each eye's blind spot is filled in by the brain and the other eye.

blocks.h: The eye is like a camera that focuses itself, adjusts its own exposure and corrects its own colors. But the one who truly "sees" is the brain behind it that makes sense of the picture. However good the camera, without someone to read the image, it is only a pile of signals.
The retina figures come from the cell counts of human retinas by Curcio and colleagues. Individuals vary considerably; these are averages.

The human retina is "inverted": the light-sensing cells lie in the innermost layer, so light must first pass through several layers of nerve cells to reach them. The biologist Richard Dawkins argued that this is like mounting the wires in front of a camera's sensor, an example of "bad design."

Later research brought out another side: the retina's Müller glial cells act like living optical fibers that guide light to the light-sensing cells; the light-sensing cells sit right against the pigment epithelium, which supplies nutrients and recycles light-sensitive pigment; in the fovea the upper cells are pushed aside so that light falls directly on the cone cells; and the inverted structure may also have a space-saving advantage.

items.h: Light must pass through the nerve layer first, and it creates a blind spot. If you designed it from scratch, you would not do it this way.
The inverted structure gives the light-sensing cells ample nourishment and repair, with light-guiding cells and the fovea compensating. Overall, it is an ingenious trade-off.
To judge whether a design is good, we first need to fully understand what it does. Our knowledge of the eye is still growing, and both sides do well to stay open.

blocks.h: The human retina has on average about 92 million rod cells and 4.6 million cone cells, with wide individual variation.
The retina's Müller cells can guide light to the light-sensing cells; how much they contribute to actual human vision is still debated.
Humans may be able to detect a single photon. This is the result of a single study, with a success rate only slightly above guessing, and it needs more replication.

Whether the inverted retina counts as "bad design" involves judgments about function and trade-offs, not just anatomical facts. That the eye's many layers work together so intricately points to a Designer; this is a philosophical inference.
His Wisdom: The One Who Formed the Eye Sees
The psalmist answers the doubter with one simple question: how could the One who made the eye be unable to see?
He who implanted the ear, won't he hear? He who formed the eye, won't he see?
Our eyes let us see the world around us. But Jesus reminds us that there is also an inner eye, and it decides whether we live our whole lives in light or in darkness.

The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
Our physical eyes see what God has made; the eyes of our heart must be opened before we can see the Creator and the wonders of His Word.
Close your eyes for ten seconds, then slowly open them. Look at the colors, the light and shadow, and the faces in front of you, and say thank you for each one.
Reflect: This week, what have my eyes most often been fixed on? Has it drawn me closer to God, or further away?

Prayer: Lord, thank You for giving me eyes that see. Open the eyes of my heart so that I may see the wonders in Your Word, and help me look at the people around me the way You see them. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: Before reading Scripture, ask God to open my eyes, so that truth becomes the lens through which I see everything.
From man's perspective to God's perspective: Look at the same situation through God's eyes, and you will often see grace.
Give thanks in everything: Being able to see is itself a gift, every single day.

blocks.h: This week: Every night before bed, write down three graces you "saw" that day, for seven days in a row.
Quiz

quiz.q: On average, about how many rod cells are in one eye?
quiz.e: Curcio and colleagues counted about 92 million rod cells on average, plus about 4.6 million cone cells.

quiz.q: Which statement about the "inverted retina" is the fairest?
o: It has been proven to be a design error
There is no debate about it at all
Some see it as bad design, while research points to its functional trade-offs; it is still open for discussion
quiz.e: This question is still being discussed. Both sides have arguments, so humility and openness are wise.

quiz.q: What question does Psalm 94:9 use to answer the doubter?
o: He who formed the eye, won't he see?
How far can a person see?
quiz.e: The One who made the eye surely sees everything.

units.title: The Brain: The Most Complex Organ
units.sub: About 86 billion neurons weave a thinking forest inside your skull.

share.v: Don't be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

blocks.h: Your brain has about 86 billion neurons, accompanied and supported by a comparable number of glial cells.

It makes up only about two percent of your body weight, yet it uses about a fifth of your body's energy. Thinking something through, remembering a face, speaking a sentence: each is the result of countless neurons working together.
I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.
The Network of Thought

items: Neurons: Each neuron is like a tree, with many "branches" that receive messages and one long "root" that sends the signal onward.
Synapses: The junctions between neurons. One neuron can connect with thousands of others, and the number of connections in the whole brain is staggering.
Plasticity: Connections that are used often grow stronger; those used rarely grow weaker. Learning, practice and habits are all reshaping your brain.
Division of labor and teamwork: Seeing, hearing, moving, speaking, remembering and judging each have main regions, but any single task needs many regions working together.

blocks.h: The brain is like a city's road network: routes that are traveled often get widened into highways, while paths rarely used slowly grow over with grass. The thoughts and actions you repeat every day are paving the roads of your heart.
Correcting a Popular Myth

People often say that "we only use 10% of our brains," but there is no scientific basis for this. Brain imaging shows that over the course of a day nearly every region becomes active in turn; damage to any small area has effects; and since the brain consumes so much energy, the body would not sustain an organ that sat 90% idle.

One study found that in London taxi drivers the rear part of the hippocampus, which handles spatial memory, was larger than in other people, and the longer they had been driving, the larger this region was. It is a famous example of the brain changing through use.
The human brain has about 86 billion neurons, with a comparable number of non-neuronal cells.
The brain makes up about 2% of body weight but consumes about 20% of the body's energy.
"We only use 10% of our brains" is an unfounded myth.
The brain changes its structure through learning and experience; the taxi driver study shows a correlation, and the detailed causal mechanisms are still being researched.

Whether mind, consciousness and moral sense can be fully explained by the physical activity of neurons is a philosophical question. That such a finely tuned thinking organ points to a wise Creator is a philosophical inference.
His Wisdom: Renewing Our Minds
God made a brain that can change, and He calls us to change. The Bible says that transformation of life begins with the renewing of the mind:
Don't be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

This does not mean the Bible is teaching neuroscience; rather, the two echo each other: God made human beings able to be renewed. More importantly, we are not changed by our own cleverness. We receive a new center for our thinking:
"For who has known the mind of the Lord, that he should instruct him?" But we have Christ's mind.
The brain is the most finely crafted tool God has given us, but it needs a Master. Only when the mind of Christ is in charge does this tool fulfill God's original purpose.
Be still for one minute and notice the thoughts coming to mind. Hand them over to God one by one.
Reflect: What thoughts do I repeat most often? What kind of roads are they paving in my heart?
Prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for making my mind. Renew my thinking, remove my wrong beliefs, and let Your truth become a highway within me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Change your mindset, change your life: Behavior is rooted in beliefs. Only when our beliefs are renewed does life truly change.
The eight steps of changing our mindset: information, revelation, conviction, practice, review, correction, repetition, multiplication. "Repetition" is exactly what paves new roads in the brain.
Lean on the Holy Spirit with your heart: The mind is a good tool, but don't use it to rely on yourself; rely with your heart on the Holy Spirit's guidance.

blocks.h: This week: Choose one Bible verse and recite it every morning and evening this week, so that truth becomes a well-traveled road in your heart.
Quiz

quiz.q: About how many neurons does the human brain have?
quiz.e: The 2009 count by Azevedo and colleagues came to about 86 billion.

quiz.q: Is it true that "we only use 10% of our brains"?
o: No, nearly every brain region becomes active
quiz.e: This is a popular myth; imaging studies and brain injury cases both show that every region of the brain has a function.

quiz.q: According to Romans 12:2, how is life transformed?
o: By the renewing of your mind
quiz.e: "Be transformed by the renewing of your mind": change begins with how we think.

units.title: The Heart: The Pump That Never Rests
units.sub: Without any reminder from you, it began beating before you were born and has never taken a break.

share.v: I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.

blocks.h: Place your hand on your chest and feel that steady beat. Your heart is only about the size of your fist.
At about 70 beats per minute, it beats roughly 100,000 times a day; live to 80, and it will beat about 3 billion times. At rest, it sends about 5 liters of blood around your body every minute.
He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber. Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The Heart's Electrical System

items: The sinoatrial (SA) node: A natural pacemaker in the right atrium that fires electrical signals on its own at a regular rhythm.
The atrioventricular (AV) node: Here the signal is deliberately delayed by about a tenth of a second, so the atria can first squeeze blood into the ventricles.
The bundle of His and Purkinje fibers: Like high-speed cables, they spread the signal rapidly through both ventricles, so the ventricles contract powerfully almost at the same moment.
Four valves: Like one-way doors, they make sure blood flows in only one direction.

blocks.h: The heart is like a symphony orchestra: the SA node is the conductor, and the AV node is like the conductor's pause, letting each section come in at the right moment. Without that one beat of waiting, the whole piece would fall apart.

The heart's rhythm is generated by the heart itself; it does not need the brain to give an order every time. Nerves and hormones only speed it up or slow it down. That is why your heart beats faster when you exercise and slower when you sleep.

It used to be thought that adult heart muscle cells never renew. A 2009 study using carbon-14 dating found that heart muscle cells do renew slowly: about 1% per year at age 25, dropping to about 0.45% at age 75.
The heartbeat starts spontaneously in the SA node and, after a delay in the AV node, passes to the ventricles. This electrical conduction system is basic physiology.
At about 70 beats per minute, a lifetime of heartbeats can reach about 3 billion; actual numbers vary from person to person.
Adult heart muscle cells renew slowly; the exact rate is still being researched and debated.
Electrical signals, delays, valves and muscle must work together precisely for the heart to keep working for a lifetime. That this points to purposeful design is a philosophical inference.
His Faithfulness: He Who Keeps You Will Not Slumber
When you fall asleep, your heart stays awake. Even more wonderful, the God who holds your life is more faithful than your heartbeat.
In the Bible, "heart" usually does not mean the physical organ but the inner center of a person: the source of our thoughts, emotions and will.
Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
Our problems are, in the end, heart problems. God's promise is not just a repair job but a brand-new heart:
I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.
Place your hand on your chest for one minute. With every beat you feel, remember one instance of God's care.
Reflect: Lately, has my heart been a soft heart of flesh, or is it slowly hardening into a heart of stone?
Prayer: Faithful Lord, thank You for keeping my heart beating until today. Take away the hardness in my heart and give me a soft heart that loves You and loves others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: The heart is the throne of life. When Jesus sits on it, the outcome of our lives will be good.
920 (the nine fruits of the Spirit, lived out in relationships): Live the self-emptied life in your relationships, and let the nine fruits of the Spirit grow from your heart.
The order of relationships: God → self → others → tasks. Give your heart to God first, and your other relationships will fall into line.

blocks.h: This week: Each morning when you get up, put your hand on your chest and say: "Lord, please reign in my heart today."
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the heart's natural pacemaker called?
quiz.e: The SA node, in the right atrium, spontaneously produces regular electrical signals.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of the AV node's delay?
o: To let the atria first squeeze blood into the ventricles
quiz.e: The delay of about a tenth of a second keeps the contractions of the atria and ventricles in proper order.

quiz.q: What does Ezekiel 36:26 promise God will give us?
o: A new heart and a new spirit
quiz.e: God will take away the stony heart and give us a heart of flesh.

units.title: The Immune System: The Body's Guard
units.sub: Patrolling day and night, telling friend from foe, and remembering every encounter.

share.v: Yahweh will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul.

blocks.h: Every breath you take and every bite you eat brings in countless microbes. Yet most of the time you are perfectly fine, because an invisible guard is patrolling your body day and night.
Even more amazing, this army learns and remembers. One study found that 25 to 75 years after smallpox vaccination, more than 90% of people still had substantial immunity.
Yahweh will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul.
Two Lines of Defense

items: Innate immunity: Skin and mucous membranes are the city walls; phagocytes, complement and inflammation are the patrols who arrive first, starting the fight within minutes to hours.
Adaptive immunity: B cells make specific antibodies, and T cells recognize and clear out infected cells. It takes a few days to prepare, but its attack is remarkably precise.
Immune memory: After a battle, "memory cells" remain, so the next time the same enemy shows up, the response is faster and stronger. Vaccines use exactly this principle.
Telling friend from foe: As the guards develop, they are trained not to attack the body's own cells.

blocks.h: The immune system is like a city: the walls keep most enemies out, patrols are ready to go at any moment, special forces deal with specific enemies, and the records office files away every enemy's face so it can be recognized at a glance next time.

We have a limited number of genes, yet we can produce an enormous variety of antibodies and receptors. The secret is that as B cells and T cells mature, they reshuffle several sets of gene segments, like building countless shapes from a limited set of building blocks.

Immunity has to be just right: too weak, and infections run out of control; too strong, or aimed at the wrong target, and allergies or autoimmune diseases result. The body has many regulating mechanisms that make this army both brave and restrained.
The immune system is divided into innate and adaptive immunity; adaptive immunity is specific and has memory.
B cells and T cells produce an enormous diversity of receptors through the recombination of gene segments.
Decades after smallpox vaccination, most people still retain antibodies or cellular immunity; T-cell responses decline slowly, with an estimated half-life of about 8 to 15 years.
That a defense system able to learn, remember, tell friend from foe and exercise restraint reflects the wisdom and care of a Creator is a philosophical inference.
His Goodness: The God Who Watches Over Us
God placed guards within our bodies; this is part of His everyday care. The Bible uses the picture of a mother bird spreading her wings to describe God's protection:
He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.

This is not a promise that believers will never get sick. It is a promise that in health or in weakness, His faithfulness surrounds us like a shield, and He is with us in our going out and our coming in.
Yahweh will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul. Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forward, and forever more.
The church is also like a body, whose members care for one another:
When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
Think about how many battles your body has quietly won this year that you never even knew about. Thank God for them.
Reflect: Spiritually, can I tell the difference between truth and lies?

Prayer: Lord who watches over me, thank You for placing guards in my body, and thank You for covering me with Your wings. Help me tell truth from lies, and make me a member of the body who cares for others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: Like immune memory, store God's Word in your heart, so you recognize a lie the moment it shows up.
235 comrades in arms (one of the three kinds of spiritual relationships): Don't fight alone. Find companions who pray for and remind one another.
Humility overcomes pride: The guards don't attack their own; neither should we treat our brothers and sisters as enemies.

blocks.h: This week: Find a comrade in arms, share one need with each other this week, and pray for each other.
Quiz

quiz.q: What are the two main parts of the immune system?
o: The brain and the spinal cord
Red blood cells and white blood cells
quiz.e: Innate immunity is fast and broad; adaptive immunity is precise and has memory.

quiz.q: Which feature of the immune system do vaccines mainly use?
quiz.e: Vaccines let the body build memory cells in advance, so it responds faster when the real enemy arrives.

quiz.q: What picture does Psalm 91:4 use to describe God's protection?
quiz.e: "He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge."

units.title: Blood Clotting: A Precise Chain Reaction
units.sub: Stopping the bleeding right at the wound, without clotting at random inside the vessels: it is a precision relay race.

share.v: But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.

blocks.h: You cut your finger on a piece of paper, it bleeds a little, and a few minutes later it stops. You hardly give it a second thought.

But think about it: if blood clotted too slowly, a small cut could bleed without stopping; if it clotted too readily, clots would form all through your blood vessels, causing strokes or heart attacks. Every day your body walks this precise tightrope.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood. I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.
Stopping Bleeding in Three Steps

items: Vessel constriction: The injured blood vessel first tightens to reduce bleeding.
Platelet plug: Platelets stick to the break and cluster together, making a temporary patch.

The clotting cascade: A chain of clotting factors is switched on in sequence, each step amplifying the next, until thrombin is produced. Thrombin turns fibrinogen into fibrin, which weaves a net that holds the patch firmly in place.
The braking system: Antithrombin, protein C and other mechanisms confine the clot to the wound; once the wound heals, the fibrinolytic system clears the clot away.

blocks.h: Clotting is like a row of ever-larger dominoes: the first small domino falls and knocks over a slightly bigger one, which knocks over a bigger one still, and very quickly a huge force builds up. But standing beside this row are many guards, making sure it falls only where it should.
In 1964, Macfarlane, and separately Davie and Ratnoff, proposed that clotting is a "waterfall" or cascade of enzyme amplification, in which one molecule can activate many molecules.

Later scholars proposed a "cell-based" model: clotting takes place on cell surfaces in stages of initiation, amplification and propagation, which better explains why clots form only at the wound. If a single factor is missing (in hemophilia, for example, factor VIII or IX), the whole system is thrown off balance.
Clotting is a chain of enzymes activated in sequence, amplifying layer upon layer.
Clotting takes place mainly on cell surfaces in stages; this model is widely accepted, and details are still being filled in.

There are differing views on how the clotting system originated: Behe argues it is "irreducibly complex"; Doolittle and colleagues point out that jawless vertebrates such as lampreys have clotting systems missing some factors, and argue it could have formed step by step.
That a system able both to amplify rapidly and to apply multiple brakes points to intelligent design is a philosophical inference.

items.h: Behe argues that without its key parts the clotting system cannot work, so it is hard to see how it could have evolved step by step.
Doolittle and colleagues, comparing the genes of different animals, point out that simpler clotting systems can also work, and argue it could have formed step by step.
Whichever view one holds about the mechanism, this precise system speaks of God's wisdom. Unity in the essentials, charity in the non-essentials.

blocks.h: His Wisdom: Grace Within Limits
God set limits for the sea, and He set limits for clotting too. Stopping exactly enough, no more and no less, is both wisdom and grace.
and said, 'Here you may come, but no further. Here your proud waves shall be stayed'?
Clotting stops our blood from flowing; yet Jesus poured out His precious blood for us, so that our sins could be forgiven.
According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.
But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.
Look at a place on your hand that was once hurt and has now healed, and remember how your body stopped the bleeding for you.
Reflect: Jesus bled and was wounded for me. What does that mean for my life today?

Prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for designing a precise system in my body to stop bleeding, and even more, thank You for pouring out Your precious blood for me, so that I have peace and healing. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus receive all the glory: That I am forgiven and healed is entirely because of His wounds, not because of my merit.
Lay down your life: Jesus shed His blood and gave His life for me; I learn to give of myself for others too.
Just the right measure: Just as clotting has both an accelerator and a brake, our words and actions need a sense of proportion, neither excessive nor indifferent.

blocks.h: This week: In one strained relationship this week, be the first to say a word of forgiveness or apology, so the wound can begin to stop bleeding.
Quiz

quiz.q: What forms in the final step of blood clotting?
quiz.e: Thrombin turns fibrinogen into fibrin, which weaves a net that holds the clot in place.

quiz.q: Why does the clotting system need "brakes"?
o: To keep clots from forming where they shouldn't
quiz.e: Anticoagulant and clot-dissolving mechanisms make sure clotting happens only at the wound.

quiz.q: What is this unit's approach to the origin of the clotting system?
o: There is only one correct view
Present the differing views side by side: unity in the essentials, charity in the non-essentials
quiz.e: Whatever our view of the mechanism, we can praise God's wisdom together.

units.title: Embryonic Development: Fearfully and Wonderfully Made
units.sub: From a single invisible cell to a person who laughs and cries.

share.v: I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.

blocks.h: You were once just a single cell, smaller than the point of a needle, only about a tenth of a millimeter across.
Today your body is estimated to have about 37 trillion cells, making up your bones, heart, eyes and brain. It all began with that one cell.
For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my mother's womb.
From One to Trillions

items: Week one: The fertilized egg divides into two, then four, forming a ball of cells that travels all the way to the uterus and implants.
Week three: Three germ layers form, which will later become, respectively, skin and nerves; muscle, bone and blood; and the digestive and respiratory organs.
Around day 22: The primitive heart begins to beat.
End of week eight: The basic outlines of the major organs have largely appeared; the fetal period follows, as the baby keeps growing and maturing.

blocks.h: Every cell carries the same "recipe book" (DNA), but heart cells open only the pages for making a heart, and eye cells read only the pages for making an eye. One book, read in different ways, makes a whole person.
These timings are the general descriptions found in embryology textbooks; each embryo varies slightly.

How does a cell know where it is, what it should become and when to stop growing? This involves complex signaling molecules and genetic switches, and it remains one of the most active research areas in developmental biology.
The human body is made up of tens of trillions of cells; a commonly cited estimate is about 37 trillion.
The human embryo's heart begins beating at around the start of the fourth week after fertilization.
How the embryo precisely controls the shape and size of each organ still holds many unanswered questions.
That a single cell unfolds on its own into a complete human being, through precise and orderly steps, points to a Creator with a plan; this is a philosophical inference.
His Wisdom and Beauty: Woven in Secret
Three thousand years ago, the psalmist knew nothing of cells or genes, yet in the language of poetry he described the mystery of being shaped in the womb:

My frame wasn't hidden from you, when I was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth. Your eyes saw my body. In your book they were all written, the days that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of them.
The word translated "woven together" carries the sense of weaving or embroidering in the original language. You were not thrown together at random; you were carefully woven.
You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
Before you were ever formed, God already knew you:
Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. Before you were born, I sanctified you. I have appointed you a prophet to the nations.
Look at your hands and your face, and say to yourself: "I was carefully woven by God."
Reflect: Do I often look down on myself? How is the way God sees me different from the way I see myself?

Prayer: Lord who made me, I give You thanks, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Heal the part of me that belittles myself; let me see myself through Your eyes and treasure every life. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: From man's perspective to God's perspective: My worth is not in my looks or my performance, but in the fact that God made me with His own hands and knows me.
People matter more than tasks: Every life, starting from the very smallest, is precious to God.
Give thanks in everything: Thank God for your body and your life, and be grateful to your parents for bringing you into the world and raising you.

blocks.h: This week: Write a thank-you card to your parents, or to whoever raised you, thanking them for bringing you into this world.
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the commonly cited estimate of the number of cells in an adult body?
quiz.e: Bianconi and colleagues estimated in 2013 about 3.72 × 10<sup>13</sup>, that is, about 37 trillion.

quiz.q: When does the embryo's heart begin to beat?
quiz.e: The primitive heart begins to beat at the start of the fourth week, one of the earliest organs to function.

quiz.q: According to Psalm 139:14, how are we made?
quiz.e: "I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made."

units.title: Wound Healing and Repair
units.sub: While you sleep, your body's repair crew is still working overtime.

share.v: It is because of Yahweh's loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn't fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

blocks.h: Your body replaces about 330 billion cells every day, weighing about 80 grams in total, most of them blood cells and cells lining the gut. You don't feel it, but this construction work never stops.
You fall and scrape your skin; a few days later it scabs over, and a few weeks later you can hardly tell. Even a broken bone can grow back together.
He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.
Three Kinds of Repair

items: Wound healing: Broadly passes through three stages: inflammation (clearing the battlefield), new tissue formation (filling in and covering over) and remodeling (strengthening the structure).
DNA repair: DNA in the body is constantly damaged by processes such as hydrolysis and oxidation, and cells have several repair systems that check and mend it at all times.
Fracture healing: First a hematoma forms, then a soft callus of cartilage and a hard callus of bone, and finally remodeling; what is rebuilt is real bone.

blocks.h: The body is like a city with maintenance crews working in shifts around the clock: some clear away rubble, some lay new roads, some inspect every electrical line and fix any damage the moment they find it.

Tomas Lindahl and two other scientists who studied these DNA repair mechanisms received the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He pointed out that DNA is in fact chemically unstable and depends on repair systems to stay intact.

Repair is not always perfect: adult wounds often leave scars, while fetal tissue in early pregnancy can regenerate without scarring; about one in ten fractures heals poorly. The body's repair is a grace, and it also reminds us that this body is still wasting away.
Wound healing includes stages of inflammation, new tissue formation and remodeling, and it is one of the most complex biological processes in the human body.
DNA in the body suffers continual chemical damage and is mended by dedicated repair systems.
About 330 billion cells are renewed in the human body each day; this is an estimate combining multiple data sources.
The process of fracture healing recapitulates many steps of embryonic skeletal development.
That the body has multiple built-in layers of self-repair reflects the faithfulness and care of the Creator; this is a philosophical inference.
His Faithfulness: New Every Morning
Your body quietly renews itself every day, as if to proclaim that God's mercies are renewed day by day:
It is because of Yahweh's loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn't fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
Yet the body will eventually grow old. The Bible tells us that the outer self wastes away, but the inner self can be renewed day by day:
Therefore we don't faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.
God does not only repair bodies; He heals broken hearts. Some wounds cannot be seen, and He can bind those up too.
Recall an experience that once hurt you and has now gradually healed, and thank God for His healing.
Reflect: Which wound in my heart still needs to be handed over to God to bind up?
Prayer: Lord who heals me, thank You for repairing my body day by day. Heal the wounds in my heart as well, so that my inner self is renewed day by day. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Life first, then relationships, then ministry: Let God restore my life first, and my relationships and service will be healthy.
Review and correction: The review and correction steps in the eight steps of changing our mindset are like a daily spiritual repair project.
235 spiritual companions (one of the three kinds of spiritual relationships): A wound has to be seen before it can be cared for; share your burdens with a trustworthy companion.

blocks.h: This week: Each night before bed, take three minutes to look back over the day, confess to God and receive His forgiveness, so every morning is a fresh start.
Quiz

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three stages of wound healing?
quiz.e: The three stages are inflammation, new tissue formation and remodeling.

quiz.q: For what area of research did Lindahl and his colleagues win the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry?
quiz.e: They showed how cells repair damaged DNA.

quiz.q: According to 2 Corinthians 4:16, what happens to our inward person?
o: It is renewed day by day
quiz.e: "Though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day."

units.title: Hands and Voice: Made to Serve and Praise
units.sub: Hands that can work and a mouth that can speak are made for serving people and praising God.

share.v: Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!

blocks.h: One hand has 27 bones. It can thread a needle and lift heavy loads; it can write and play the piano, and it can help up someone who has fallen.
To say a single sentence, you coordinate more than a hundred muscles of the larynx, mouth, face and breathing, so fast that you are not even aware of it.
Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!
Hands That Work, a Mouth That Speaks

items: The opposable thumb: The human thumb can meet the pads of the other fingers, letting us pinch, turn and hold with fine control.
Two kinds of grip: The anatomist Napier distinguished the "power grip" (like holding a hammer) from the "precision grip" (like holding a pen); the human hand has both.
The voice system: The lungs supply airflow, the vocal cords vibrate to make sound, and the tongue, lips and palate shape the sound into words.
Language: With a limited number of words, people can build an infinite number of sentences that have never been spoken before.

blocks.h: The hand is like an all-purpose toolbox: the same set of tools can do heavy work and delicate work. The voice is like a pipe organ: as air flows through different pipes and stops, it plays an endless variety of musical phrases.
The human ability to grip makes tools, art and caring for others possible.

Linguists debate what is unique about human language. Hauser, Chomsky and Fitch suggest that the ability to combine words layer upon layer into infinitely many sentences may be the core feature of human language; this view is still under academic discussion.
Each hand has 27 bones, including the carpals, metacarpals and phalanges.
Speaking requires coordinating more than a hundred muscles of the larynx, mouth, face and breathing.
The human hand is capable of both the power grip and the precision grip.
Which features of human language are unique to humans is still being debated by scholars.
That humans have been given hands and mouths able to create, communicate and praise points to a Creator who wants a relationship with us; this is a philosophical inference.
His Beauty: Made to Praise
Our hands and mouths are not accidental accessories; they are for responding to God's love. Moses prayed like this:
Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us. Yes, establish the work of our hands.
We are God's workmanship, made to do good works:
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.
The most beautiful use of our lips is to praise God:
Through him, then, let's offer up a sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips which proclaim allegiance to his name.
Having walked through the whole Human Body Hall, we can see it now: eyes, brain, heart, blood, hands and mouth are all gifts from God. The most fitting response is to offer our whole body to Him.
Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.

Or don't you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's.
Lift up both your hands and use your voice to sing a hymn (for example, "Amazing Grace"), or read Psalm 150 out loud.
Reflect: What did my hands do this week? What did my mouth say? Did they glorify God and bless others?
Prayer: Lord who made me, I offer You my eyes, my mind, my heart, my hands and my mouth. May all the work and words of my life become a sacrifice of praise to You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus receive all the glory: The skill of our hands and the power of our mouths are gifts; all we accomplish belongs to Him.
Build God's kingdom system: Use my hands to serve in my family, workplace and church, so that God's purposes are fulfilled.
Become an overcomer: Offer your body as a living sacrifice, serving with your hands and praising with your mouth every day.

blocks.h: This week: Use your hands this week to do one concrete act of service for someone, and use your mouth to speak a word of blessing to them.

Congratulations on completing the Human Body Hall! From eyes that see the light to a voice that lifts up praise, you have seen that you are fearfully and wonderfully made, and you have come to know the God who made you with His own hands and watches over you every day.
Quiz

quiz.q: How many bones are in one hand?
quiz.e: They include 8 carpal bones, 5 metacarpal bones and 14 phalanges.

quiz.q: About how many muscles must be coordinated to speak?
quiz.e: Simonyan and Horwitz point out that speaking requires coordinating more than a hundred muscles of the larynx, mouth, face and breathing.

quiz.q: According to Hebrews 13:15, what is "the fruit of lips"?
o: A sacrifice of praise offered to God
quiz.e: "Let's offer up a sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips which proclaim allegiance to his name."

units.title: Sleep: God’s Gift of Rest
units.sub: Every night, even the busiest person has to hand over the steering wheel, and that fact is itself a lesson.

share.v: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

quiz.q: What does the consensus recommendation on adult sleep (AASM and SRS, 2015) say?
o: Regularly sleep 7 or more hours per night
quiz.e: The statement addresses adults aged 18 to 60 and recommends regularly sleeping 7 or more hours; individual needs still vary.

quiz.q: What is the current scientific status of the idea that “the brain clears waste during sleep”?
o: It is completely settled and no one disagrees
It has been proven completely wrong
It comes mainly from animal experiments and is still debated
quiz.e: Mouse studies from 2013 and 2024 point in opposite directions, and the methods on both sides are still under discussion.

quiz.q: When Elijah in the Bible was exhausted and even asked to die, what did God do first?
o: Rebuked him for not having enough faith
Let him sleep and sent an angel with food
Told him to go straight back to work
quiz.e: First Kings 19 records that God first cared for his body and did not begin by rebuking him.

blocks.h: At our present rhythm of life, a person who lives to eighty will spend about 25 years lying with eyes closed. During that time you earn no money, answer no messages, and may not even hear your own name when it is called.

From an engineering point of view, this design seems absurd: a creature that can be hunted and has deadlines to meet shuts itself down for a third of every day. Yet no one can skip it for long. Presidents, surgeons and the hardest-driving entrepreneurs all have to hand over the steering wheel every night.
It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.
A few journeys in one night

In 1953 Eugene Aserinsky and Nathaniel Kleitman at the University of Chicago noticed that after people fall asleep, their eyes move rapidly at regular intervals. This was the discovery of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, and it overturned the notion that sleep is the brain simply stopping work.

A night of sleep is made up of several cycles. One cycle lasts about 90 to 110 minutes and repeats 4 to 6 times through the night. Non-REM sleep (NREM) is divided into N1, N2 and N3 and makes up about three quarters of the night, with REM about a quarter. There is more deep sleep (N3) in the first half of the night, and the nearer morning comes, the longer REM lasts.

Think of sleep as a factory that runs through the night. The first half of the night is the cleaning and maintenance shift, when the machines are stopped for servicing. In the second half the filing and creativity shift takes over, sorting the papers piled on the desk during the day and connecting a few wires at random, which is why you have such strange dreams. An analogy is not a mechanism; this is only to help you remember that the body is not idle while you sleep.
The price of too little sleep

In 2015 a consensus statement from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) and the Sleep Research Society (SRS) recommended that adults aged 18 to 60 regularly sleep 7 or more hours per night for optimal health. Regularly sleeping less than 7 hours is associated with weight gain, diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease, stroke, depression, weakened immunity and a higher risk of accidents. “Associated with” does not mean that every item has been proven to be causal.

In a 2000 Australian study, 39 transport workers and military personnel were tested: after 17 to 19 hours of continuous wakefulness, their performance on some tests was equal to or worse than at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05%. The danger of driving after staying up late is often underestimated by the driver.
Memory is sorted at night

A large body of research shows that sleep helps consolidate what we learned during the day. A major 2013 review in Physiological Reviews sorted out the roles of NREM and REM sleep in memory. The detailed mechanisms are still being studied, but the evidence is fairly consistent that an all-nighter before an exam does not pay off.
The brain’s night cleaning crew?

In 2013 the team of Maiken Nedergaard reported in Science that in mice the brain clears metabolites faster during sleep than during wakefulness. This picture of the “glymphatic system” quickly became popular. In 2024 a team led by Nicholas Franks and colleagues reported the opposite in Nature Neuroscience: in their mouse experiments, clearance was lower during sleep and anesthesia. In 2025 Nedergaard’s team reported in Cell that slow oscillations of norepinephrine drive the constriction and dilation of blood vessels, which propels cerebrospinal fluid flow during NREM sleep.

items.h: Tracer and imaging studies show enhanced cerebrospinal fluid flow and waste clearance during sleep; the rhythmic pulsation of blood vessels may be the driving force.

Experiments that directly track fluorescent molecules in the brain found higher clearance during wakefulness, and earlier results may have been affected by the way they were measured. Critics, in turn, question the injection volumes and analysis methods of such experiments.

blocks.h: This debate has not been resolved, and most of the data come from mice. The claim on the market that “sleep detoxes your brain” has run ahead of the evidence.
Let’s separate what is certain, what is under discussion, and what is inference.
Human sleep has cyclical NREM and REM stages; REM was first reported in 1953 by Aserinsky and Kleitman.

The AASM and SRS consensus statement recommends that adults aged 18 to 60 regularly sleep 7 or more hours; the ACP guideline recommends cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) as the initial treatment for chronic insomnia.

Chronic short sleep is associated with many chronic diseases and with accident risk; after 17 to 19 hours of continuous wakefulness, performance on some tests is similar to a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05%. The extent of causation and individual differences are still under discussion.
Sleep helps consolidate memory; the specific mechanisms are still being studied.
Whether sleep enhances the brain’s waste clearance remains disputed; mouse studies from 2013 to 2025 have reached different conclusions and cannot be applied directly to humans.

The fact that humans must sleep can be read as a mark of creaturely limitation: a body that God designed reminds us every day that the world does not run on our own effort. This is a reading of faith; physiology itself will not tell you this.
The One who does not slumber
The Bible puts the difference between humans and God on the pillow: people must sleep every day, and God does not.
He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber. Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.

God’s goodness is here too. He could have made people into tools that never need rest, but He wrote rest into the rhythm of the body, and on the seventh day of creation He Himself established the Sabbath. Sleep is a small daily Sabbath, in which we do nothing and the sun comes up all the same.
And then the Lord who never slumbers became a man. When the storm broke, He was asleep in the stern on the cushion. He knows what weariness tastes like.
He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and asked him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”

This Lord who knows weariness later said “It is finished” on the cross, completing the work that we could never finish by ourselves. That is why He can invite people to come to Him for rest; the foundation of this rest is His finished work, not whether we slept well tonight.
“Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

If you are suffering from insomnia, hear this: Psalm 127 is not a faith exam. David also wept every night, and Asaph said to God, “You hold my eyelids open.” Being unable to sleep does not mean God does not love you, and it does not mean your faith is lacking.
Tonight when you lie down, put your phone a little farther away, and slowly name the things you did not finish today, one by one. After each one, say: “Lord, tonight I give this to You.”
Meditate: Which matter do I find hardest to let go of? Do I secretly believe that the moment I close my eyes, the world will go wrong?

Pray: Lord who neither slumbers nor sleeps, thank You for designing my body, and thank You that You still watch over me in the night. I place my unfinished work and my unresolved worries into Your hands. Give me rest; and if I still find it hard to sleep tonight, be with me and give me wisdom to seek the help I need. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility overcomes pride: Going to bed on time is a concrete form of humility. It admits that the world does not run on me, and lets God be God and people be people.
Jesus is my example: He slept on the boat, and He also took His disciples away to rest a while. The Lord did not squeeze people dry to accomplish ministry.

People matter more than tasks: Life first, then relationships, then ministry. Do not give up your body and your family’s smiles for results bought with late nights, and do not expect coworkers to be on call at all hours.

blocks.h: This week: For seven days in a row, fix your wake-up time and keep your phone where you cannot reach it from bed. If insomnia lasts for weeks, if it clearly affects your days, or if family members notice that you snore and stop breathing in your sleep, please see a doctor; chronic insomnia has evidence-based treatments such as CBT-I. This unit is not medical advice.
Pass it on: Have you been sleeping well lately? When you wake in the middle of the night, what is usually going around in your mind?
Quiz

units.title: The Ear and Balance: The Miracle of Hearing
units.sub: The eye has eyelids; the ear has none. This delicate organ keeps its door open even while you sleep, and it even makes sounds of its own.

share.v: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.

blocks.h: Your ears make sounds of their own. This is not a figure of speech. In 1978 the British scientist David Kemp placed a sensitive microphone in a person’s ear canal, played a short sound into it, and recorded an echo coming back out of the ear. Today the hearing screening of many newborns works by listening for this echo.

Now try a small experiment: stare at this line of text and shake your head quickly from side to side. The words stay clear. Now hold your head still and wave your phone quickly from side to side, and the words blur. What keeps the words steady when you shake your head is also hidden in your ear.
He who implanted the ear, won’t he hear? He who formed the eye, won’t he see?
A relay race

Sound is only vibration in the air. It travels into the ear canal and pushes on the eardrum, which hands it to three tiny bones: the malleus, the incus and the stapes. The stapes is the smallest bone in the human body. These three bones amplify the vibration and pass it on to the fluid-filled cochlea of the inner ear.

The cochlea is shaped like a snail shell, and the basilar membrane inside rises and falls with the vibration, forming a traveling wave. The Hungarian-born scientist Georg von Békésy won the 1961 Nobel Prize for working out the physical mechanism of the cochlea. High tones peak near the entrance of the cochlea and low tones travel deeper, so the cochlea lays out a musical scale along its length.

The cochlea is like a piano rolled up into a spiral, with the keys running from high notes to low. The difference is that a piano needs someone to play it, while in the cochlea the whole length of the strings rises and falls with the sound wave, and each tone sounds most strongly at its own place. When you hear a chord, several places on this piano are moving at once.
Fifteen thousand on duty

What really turns vibration into electrical signals are the hair cells. Each cochlea has only about 3,500 inner hair cells and 12,000 outer hair cells, strikingly few compared with the hundreds of millions of photoreceptors in the retina. When the tiny hairs on top of a hair cell bend, channels at their tips open, chemicals rush in, and the signal travels up the auditory nerve.

The outer hair cells have one more remarkable job. In 1985 William Brownell and colleagues found that isolated outer hair cells lengthen and shorten by themselves when stimulated. They act like a row of tiny motors that boost weak vibrations, which makes the ear an active amplifier. The echo that Kemp recorded is a trace left by this active mechanism.
The spirit level in your ear

The inner ear also houses the vestibular system. The three semicircular canals are roughly perpendicular to one another and detect rotation of the head; the otolith organs sense gravity and straight-line acceleration. Like the cochlea, they use hair cells, and they send their information quickly to the neural circuits that control the eyes and muscles. So when you shake your head, your eyes compensate in the opposite direction, and the words stay steady.
When hearing is damaged

World Health Organization data from 2026: about 430 million people worldwide have disabling hearing loss, including 34 million children. By 2050 it is projected that more than 700 million people will have disabling hearing loss and nearly 2.5 billion will have some degree of hearing loss. More than 1 billion young people are at risk of preventable permanent hearing loss from unsafe listening habits.

Cochlear implants bypass the damaged part and stimulate the auditory nerve directly. Data from the US National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders say that as of December 2019, about 736,900 implant devices had been registered worldwide. They help many people understand speech, but they are not the same as restoring normal hearing, and learning to use them takes time. The Deaf community also has its own rich language and culture; sign language is a complete language, and people who cannot hear are in no way lesser people.
This unit is not medical advice. If you have sudden hearing loss, persistent ringing in the ears or repeated dizziness, please see an ear, nose and throat doctor promptly.
Where did the ear come from?

Mainstream biology holds that the middle ear bones of mammals evolved from jaw bones of their ancestors, and both fossils and embryonic development offer clues. Christians differ on the manner and timing of creation, so the views are set side by side below.

items.h: God made the ear through a long natural process. The repurposing of bones does not diminish His wisdom; it is rather like a craftsman who uses old materials with extraordinary skill.
Gradual evolution is enough to explain the ear’s delicacy without a designer; the ear also has weaknesses, for example that damaged hair cells in humans are hard to regenerate.

The interlocking parts of the ear show God’s direct design; these thinkers interpret the fossil evidence differently. This is a minority position that the scientific community generally does not accept.

blocks.h: Separating what is certain from what is inferred is the only way to do justice to this subject.
Each human cochlea has about 3,500 inner hair cells and 12,000 outer hair cells (figures often cited in textbooks; individuals vary).
The cochlea distinguishes frequencies by position; Békésy won the 1961 Nobel Prize for the physical mechanism of stimulation within the cochlea.
Outer hair cells can actively lengthen and shorten, the ear has an active amplification mechanism, and it can emit otoacoustic emissions that can be recorded.
WHO data for 2026: about 430 million people have disabling hearing loss, projected to exceed 700 million by 2050.
Cochlear implants help many people understand speech; results vary from person to person, and they are not the same as restoring normal hearing.

This delicate system makes us marvel at the Creator’s wisdom. That is an interpretation of faith and not an experimental result. An atheist biologist looking at the same pair of ears would credit them to evolution. Science describes how the ear works; whether it comes from a God who hears prayer has to be answered by looking elsewhere.
Those who are heard learn to listen

The ear has no eyelid, and sound comes in without your permission. This makes hearing an open posture. Faith begins this way too: the gospel is news that someone else tells you, which you can only accept or refuse, and which you could never have thought up by yourself.
So faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

The “hearing” here does not depend on the cochlea. Sign language, braille, and a person’s lived-out love can all bring the word of Christ into a heart. Mark records that when Jesus met a man who was deaf and could hardly speak, He first led him away from the crowd and put His fingers into his ears. While this man could not hear, He spoke to him through touch.
He took him aside from the multitude privately and put his fingers into his ears; and he spat and touched his tongue.

Isaiah describes a suffering servant who opens his ear to God every morning, and who, by the end of that listening, walks a road of humiliation. Christians see this servant in Jesus. He listened to the Father so completely that He went to the cross, so that we, who so often stop our ears, could be forgiven.

The Lord GOD has opened my ear. I was not rebellious. I have not turned back. I gave my back to those who beat me, and my cheeks to those who plucked off the hair. I didn’t hide my face from shame and spitting.

Close your eyes for a minute. Count how many sounds you can hear: the air conditioner, a car in the distance, your own breathing. Each one is caught for you by thousands of cells. Then stare at a line of text and shake your head, and thank God that He keeps you steady in the shaking.
Meditate: When did I last listen carefully while someone finished what they were saying? How much time do I leave for God in which I do not speak and only listen?

Pray: Lord who formed the ear, You hear every sigh I cannot put into words. Open my ears so that I hear Your voice and the voices of those around me. Remember my friends with hearing loss, and let them receive respect and love. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Holy Spirit is my guide: The Good Shepherd’s voice is discerned in quiet. Listen to Scripture each day first, and only then open your mouth to bring requests to God.
920, people matter more than tasks: Every relationship is a “2” in my life. Practice attentive listening as a discipline of selflessness: interrupt less, and ask one more question.
The Bible is my standard: There are many voices outside; use God’s word to recalibrate the spirit level in my heart.

blocks.h: This week: Turn your headphone volume down one notch, and find an older person or a friend with hearing difficulty. Talk for ten minutes face to face, speaking more slowly.
Pass it on: Is there a sentence someone said to you that you still remember to this day?
Quiz

quiz.q: How does the cochlea distinguish high tones from low tones?
o: Different frequencies peak at different positions
By changes in the thickness of the eardrum
quiz.e: The traveling wave that Békésy studied shows that different frequencies peak at different places on the basilar membrane.

quiz.q: What special ability do outer hair cells have?
o: They can actively lengthen and shorten, amplifying weak vibrations
quiz.e: Brownell and colleagues observed their active movement in 1985, which makes the ear an active amplifier.

quiz.q: What mainly keeps the words clear when you shake your head?
o: The eyelids opening and closing rapidly
Amplification by the middle ear bones
The vestibular system driving the eyes to compensate
quiz.e: The semicircular canals detect head rotation, and the brain has the eyes compensate in the opposite direction.

units.title: The Gut Microbiome: A Community Inside Your Body
units.sub: You think you are one person, but you are really a neighborhood. And the long-repeated claim that “bacteria outnumber you ten to one” is a wrong number.

share.v: from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.

blocks.h: After a big bowel movement, the human cells in your body may briefly become the majority. In 2016 researchers at Israel’s Weizmann Institute of Science estimated that the numbers of bacteria and human cells in the body are about equal, and that each bowel movement removes about a quarter to a third of the colon’s contents, which may flip the ratio for a while.

Mother’s milk holds another oddity: it contains large amounts of oligosaccharides that the baby cannot digest. This nourishment is meant for the good bacteria in the baby’s gut. Before the baby has learned to speak, the mother has already prepared a meal for his “neighbors.”
For the body is not one member, but many.
A corrected number

You may have heard that “the bacteria in your body outnumber your human cells ten to one.” In 2016 Ron Sender, Shai Fuchs and Ron Milo traced it and found that the claim mostly goes back to a rough estimate from the 1970s. They recalculated: a 70-kilogram adult man has about 38 trillion bacteria and 30 trillion human cells, a ratio of about 1.3:1, and the bacteria weigh only about 0.2 kilograms in total.

About 25 trillion of the human cells are red blood cells. If you count only the human cells that have a nucleus (about 3 trillion), bacteria still outnumber them by about ten to one. So the way of counting changes what you can say, and the assumptions behind a number have to be made clear.

The gut is like an old produce market. The fishmonger, the vegetable seller and the tofu vendor each run their own business, yet depend on one another: one stall’s scraps are another stall’s raw material. Whether an out-of-town vendor can get in depends on whether there is a free spot, and the look of the market shifts with what the neighbors eat. It is hard to point at any one stall and say, “The market is that one.”
The power of environment

A 2018 Israeli study in Nature analyzed data from over a thousand people and found that the gut microbiome is shaped mainly by environment: diet, medications and health status matter far more than genes. People who live in the same home but are not blood relatives have clearly similar microbiomes. Your gut also records who you eat with.
The brain and the gut are wired together, but don’t run too fast

There are neural, immune and metabolic channels of communication between the gut and the brain. A long 2019 review by John Cryan and colleagues gathered a great deal of evidence, much of it from animal experiments.

On the other side, Katarzyna Hooks and colleagues pointed out in Behavioral and Brain Sciences in 2019 that the methods and core findings of this field have rarely been rigorously examined, and that the media often treat correlation as causation. The relationships of depression and autism to gut bacteria cannot at present be called established.

items.h: Animal experiments have shown that the microbiome can influence behavior, and associations in humans keep accumulating, so developing new treatments is worthwhile.
Germ-free mice are an extreme model, and human studies are mostly correlational; disease may change diet and diet may change the microbiome, so the direction of causation is often impossible to tell.

blocks.h: Probiotics and fecal transplants

The American Gastroenterological Association’s 2020 guideline does not recommend routine use of probiotics for most digestive diseases, and gives conditional recommendations only in a few specific situations. A small 2018 study in Cell even found that people who took a multi-strain probiotic after a course of antibiotics had a delayed recovery of the gut mucosal microbiome. This does not mean all probiotics are harmful, but it reminds us that “natural” and “friendly bacteria” do not mean good for everyone.

There are real medical successes. In a 2013 randomized trial in the New England Journal of Medicine, patients with recurrent Clostridium difficile infection who received an infusion of donor stool did much better than those given antibiotics alone. This was done under medical supervision; never try it yourself. In another small Stanford study, with 18 people per group, the group that ate more fermented foods showed a rise in microbiome diversity and a drop in inflammation markers, which larger studies still need to confirm.
This unit is not medical advice. See a doctor for persistent digestive problems, and ask your physician before taking any medication or supplement.
Let’s separate what is certain from what is inferred. The gut microbiome especially needs this, because it is a favorite topic of supplement advertising.
Bacteria and human cells in the body are of the same order of magnitude, about 1.3:1; the “ten to one” claim lacks a basis. This is still an estimate, with an uncertainty of about 25%.
Human milk contains oligosaccharides that babies can hardly digest and that can serve as food for gut bacteria.
Environment and diet influence the composition of the gut microbiome far more than genes do.
For recurrent Clostridium difficile infection, fecal microbiota transplant has good evidence; for most other diseases, the benefits of probiotics are limited or uncertain.
Gut bacteria influence mood and behavior: animal experiments give signals, but causation in humans has not been established.

The interdependence of billions of tiny lives with the human body reminds Christians of the Bible’s description of the “body.” This is an analogy and a meditation; bacteria do not prove God, and evolutionary biology can also describe how symbiosis arose.
The least noticeable are the most necessary
The Bible long ago compared a community to a body. When Paul wrote to the church in Corinth, it was divided over gifts and status, and he asked them to look at their own bodies.
No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.

We cannot see the bacteria in the gut, just as no one sees the contributions of many in the church: those who clean the restrooms, those who pray for others before dawn, those who help wash the dishes. They, like the bacteria, sustain the life of the whole in places no one sees.
But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part, that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.
It is the cross that makes enemies into one body

A human community is not like the gut. Bacteria coexist through mutual benefit, but people hold grudges, feel jealousy, and drive others out of the door. Bringing Jew and Gentile into one cost Christ His own body.
and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the hostility through it.
The unity of the church does not rest on compatible personalities, nor on mutual advantage. It is built on the One who gave His body for us.

Before your next meal, look at a plate of greens and think: this meal feeds not only you but also the tens of trillions of unseen tenants inside you. Give thanks to the God who fits all things together.
Meditate: In my family or church, who is the “unseen yet indispensable” person? When did I last thank him or her?

Pray: Lord who fits the body together, thank You for placing me in a network of life larger than myself. Forgive me for so often putting myself at the center and looking down on the weaker members. Help us to care for one another, made one by the cross of Christ. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Life first, then relationships, then ministry: The church is not a machine but a living body. First care for one another, then talk about the work.
From self-centered to selfless: Stop asking, “What use is this person to me?” and ask instead, “How can I help complete others in this body?”
235 spiritual companions: A body never has just one cell. Find at least one companion to walk with, and do not fight alone.

blocks.h: This week: Thank someone who quietly serves in your church or workplace, in person, and name one specific thing they did. When you receive a forwarded message about a health supplement, check the source before you forward it.
Pass it on: Do you think a person can truly live entirely on his own? Who has influenced you most in your life?
Quiz

quiz.q: According to the 2016 estimate by Sender and colleagues, what is the approximate ratio of bacteria to human cells in the body?
quiz.e: They corrected the long-repeated ten to one; this is an estimate and still has uncertainty.

quiz.q: What is one of the main functions of the oligosaccharides in breast milk that babies cannot digest?
o: Feeding the bacteria in the baby’s gut
quiz.e: These oligosaccharides can serve as food for beneficial gut bacteria.

quiz.q: What is the most honest statement about gut bacteria affecting mood?
o: It has been proven that probiotics treat depression
Animal experiments give signals, but causation in humans has not been established
The two have no relationship at all
quiz.e: Correlation is not causation; critics also warn that the media often overstate it.

units.title: Aging: The Outer Self Decays, the Inner Self Is Renewed
units.sub: Cells have only so many tickets to punch, but a person’s hope has no limit. Science can tell us how the body ages; the Bible tells us where we are headed as we grow old.

share.v: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.

blocks.h: Today your body will replace roughly 330 billion cells. In 2021 Ron Sender and Ron Milo estimated this figure, and most of those cells are blood cells and cells lining the gut. That works out to a few million every second, so even while you read this sentence, the old is being torn down and the new put up.

A body this good at renewing itself: why does it still grow old? That question has sent people into the laboratory, and it has also brought them face to face with a sentence written two thousand years ago.
Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.
How many tickets a cell can punch

In 1961 Leonard Hayflick and Paul Moorhead published a study showing that normal human cells grown in the laboratory stop dividing after a while. This overturned the view of the day that cells could divide forever. The ceiling later became known as the Hayflick limit, commonly estimated at about 50 divisions.

Part of the reason lies at the tips of our chromosomes. There sits a repeated stretch of DNA called the telomere, and it gets a little shorter every time the cell copies itself. In 1985 Carol Greider and Elizabeth Blackburn discovered telomerase, an enzyme that can lengthen telomeres. For this work they shared the 2009 Nobel Prize with Jack Szostak.

Picture an old photocopier that chops off one line at the bottom of the page every time it copies. A clever clerk leaves several blank lines at the end of every document, so the chopping does no harm. Telomeres are like those blank lines. But the blank space eventually runs out, and the next cut goes into the actual text. That is when the cell stops.
Why not switch telomerase fully on?

It sounds simple: switch telomerase on, and wouldn’t cells live forever? The trouble is that cancer cells do exactly this. The Nobel Prize’s official explanation points out that cancer cells often have higher telomerase activity. Limiting how often cells divide may also be one of the gates the body uses to guard against cells that run out of control.
Aging has more than one cause

Telomeres are only one thread. A 2023 review in the journal Cell sorted aging into twelve hallmarks, including genomic instability, epigenetic changes, loss of protein homeostasis, cellular senescence and chronic inflammation. There is no single switch, and so there is no single cure.
Is there a limit to how long we can live? People are still arguing

In 2016 Xiao Dong and colleagues argued in Nature that human lifespan may have an upper limit, at around 115 years. In 2018 Elisabetta Barbi and colleagues studied Italian data on the very oldest people and concluded that death rates level off to a plateau after age 105, with no clear limit in sight. In 2024 S. Jay Olshansky and colleagues analyzed data from several long-lived countries and concluded that, unless aging itself is markedly slowed, radical life extension this century is implausible. They estimated that the share of people reaching 100 is unlikely to exceed 15% for women or 5% for men.

items.h: Records for long life have not kept being broken in recent decades, and the body’s ability to repair itself has limits.
Death rates flatten out at extreme old age, the data are scarce, and the record may still be broken.

blocks.h: An honest progress report on anti-aging

Animal experiments are tantalizing. A 2020 report in Nature described using three reprogramming factors to change the epigenetic state of optic nerve cells in mice, and this restored vision in aged mice and in a mouse model of glaucoma. Those were mice, not people. In humans, a 2019 open-label trial of a drug that selectively clears senescent cells enrolled 14 patients with pulmonary fibrosis. Physical ability improved, lung function did not change, and it counted only as a feasibility study. Be skeptical of any product on the market that promises to “reverse aging.”

The evolutionary view offers an explanation too, such as the “disposable soma” theory Thomas Kirkwood proposed in 1977: a living thing gives priority to its limited energy for reproduction, and body maintenance only needs to be good enough.
Growing older is not only a downhill slope

Laura Carstensen of Stanford University and her colleagues followed adults for more than ten years. They found that older adults reported higher emotional well-being and steadier emotions, and were better able to feel joy and sorrow at the same time. Joshua Hartshorne and Laura Germine analyzed nearly 50,000 online participants together with norm data. They found that different mental abilities peak at different ages: some decline early, and others do not peak until after middle age. These are trends across groups. They do not deny the real hardship that many elderly people face through illness, loneliness and dementia.
This unit is not medical advice. If your memory clearly worsens or your body changes, please see a doctor early.
Aging is the favorite topic of the anti-aging industry, which is exactly why we need to sort things out carefully.
Normal human cells divide a limited number of times in culture; the discovery of telomeres and telomerase was awarded the 2009 Nobel Prize.
Aging has many mechanisms, and no single cause.

Studies of groups show that older adults’ average emotional well-being is no lower than, and even higher than, that of younger adults, and that different mental abilities peak at different ages. Individual differences are large.
Whether human lifespan has an absolute upper limit is still debated among scholars.
Reprogramming and clearing senescent cells have produced results in animal experiments, but evidence in humans is still at an early stage. At present there is no method proven to reverse human aging.

Christians hope for the resurrection of the body. This is a declaration of faith that science can neither confirm nor deny. Its basis is the testimony to Christ’s resurrection and has nothing to do with the length of one’s telomeres.
The Bible does not lie about old age
Psalm 90 does not put makeup on aging. Moses knew how short our years are, and he asked God to teach him to count them.

The days of our years are seventy, or even by reason of strength eighty years; yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for it passes quickly, and we fly away. So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
Right after that, God makes the elderly a very tender promise: He will carry them.
Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.
The Bible also teaches us to honor the elderly. To stand up in the presence of gray hair is a command God placed exactly where society is most likely to overlook the old.
Death is not the last word

The Christian hope is not about pushing death back by a few years. Jesus truly died, was buried and rose on the third day, and Paul calls Him the “first fruit.” Once the first fruit has ripened, the harvest of the whole tree is guaranteed.
So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown perishable; it is raised imperishable. It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
So a Christian can see a doctor, exercise and thank God for medicine, and still not be frightened by growing old. Aging is not a punishment for you, and it does not mean your faith is too small.
Find a photo from ten years ago and look at it. Thank God for the road He has brought you along these ten years, and tell Him concretely the fear you have in your heart about growing old.
Meditate: what do I fear losing most when I am old? How does Jesus’ resurrection speak to this?

Prayer: Lord who carries me to old age, my outer self is decaying; please make my inner self new day by day. Comfort the elderly who are in pain and living with dementia, and the people who care for them. Thank You for rising from the dead and giving us a living hope. In the name of Jesus, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Shift from an earthly viewpoint to an eternal one: what is seen is temporary, and what is unseen is eternal. Spend less money on buying back youth and more time building lives.
Spiritual parents and children: the elderly have experience to pass on, and the young have strength to walk alongside them. Helping each other grow is the 235 relationship.
Become an overcomer: overcoming does not depend on a body that never ages. To keep loving others and giving thanks in weakness is itself a testimony.

blocks.h: This week: visit or phone an elder and ask them to tell you a story of God’s leading in their life. Write it down or record it, and give it to them.
Pass it on: what do you picture yourself like at eighty? Who do you hope will be beside you then?
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the Hayflick limit?
o: The most a person can live is 122 years
Normal human cells divide a limited number of times in culture
The number of cells a person replaces each day
quiz.e: Hayflick and Moorhead’s 1961 research overturned the view that cells can divide forever.

quiz.q: Why can’t we simply switch on telomerase to fight aging?
o: Cancer cells also often rely on telomerase to keep dividing
Telomerase has not yet been discovered
quiz.e: Limiting division may also be a gate that guards against cancer, so anti-aging is not that simple.

quiz.q: What is the foundation of the Christian hope in the face of aging?
o: Telomeres can be lengthened without limit
If your faith is great enough, you will not age
Christ has been raised from the dead and is the first fruit
quiz.e: Hope is built on Christ’s resurrection and has nothing to do with how strong the body is.

questions.q: Am I something pieced together by chance, or someone carefully woven?
If the body can repair itself, can my broken heart be healed too?
When we grow old, does life still have value?
